One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Parents pay 4500 Rands a month, but can their children read?

Summary:
Several parents from Arvenites College of Education are outraged after their children failed matrix, and independent evaluations show they are way behind in their education. Many classes are held by "teaching assistants", unqualified teachers who are family of the owners.

Further information:
14 of the 16 children of the school who wrote matrix have failed 2015 exams. They were excelling with marks between 70% and 80% up until the exams were independently set and marked.
Despite several complaints and criminal charges being laid,it;s business as usual at Arvanites

Press Release:


Independent School Investigated
No uniforms, no school bells and no homework. Promises of small classes, individual attention and fees at R4500 a month sounded idyllic for pupils and seemed the perfect solution for many parents. So how did 14 out of 16 matrics fail their final exams at an independent private Johannesburg college, despite high marks and even distinctions throughout the year? Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


ARVANITES

V/O: Small classes, individual attention, no work to be taken home. It sounds like a dream school,

Steve: We used to get reports and they were doing marvelous!

Lesley: We had nice, calm, happy kids who were getting good results.

Link: The official logo of the Arvanites College of Education is an ancient Greek symbol, a lamp of knowledge and learning.

V/O: But at the end of last year 14 out of 16 pupils failed Matric.
This privately owned, independent school in Randburg costs R4500 a month. It’s a family business run by Sheryl Arvanites, her husband Tony, her son Anthony, her sister Brenda Pieters, and Brenda’s twin daughters Kayla and Jenine. We asked Sheryl Arvanites about the poor results.

Sheryl: I cannot be responsible for those kind of results.

Bongani: Who is responsible?

Sheryl: The learners and their parents.

V/O: Lesley Moriarty had two sons at Arvanites College. Both received trophies and certificates over the years for excellent work, and Kieran passed Grade 11 with a 78% average and 3 distinctions. But in matric finals the wheels came off.

Lesley: Kieran’s prelim marks – he would have got a University exemption with it, and yet he out and out failed matric.

V/O: At the end of Grade 11 Kieran got 73% for Maths, but in the matric finals he got 6%.

Bongani: Who was the Maths teacher?

Lesley: Sheryl Arvanites taught them Maths.

Sheryl: Their appalling results at the end of the year were as a direct result of their behavior during the final matric exams.

Bongani: Hold on, are you saying that in the end they just forgot everything?

Sheryl: They didn’t forget everything they refused to write. We have got video footage that shows the learners coming into the exam writing venue late, putting their heads down and refusing to write the paper.

V/O: But the footage provided by the school contradicts this. The start of the 3-hour Maths exam shows all learners present and awake. Thirty minutes in and they are all still busy. Two hours later most of them have given up. The school also provided the invigilator’s report claiming one student refused to write, but 6 matrics emailed Carte Blanche stating they couldn’t answer the questions because they hadn’t covered the work.

Bongani: They looked at these exam papers and had no clue what was on there because you’d never taught them?

Sheryl: That’s really crazy.

V/O: Devon Lewis started at Sheryl’s small homeschool when he was 12. In September 2010 the school moved to a shopping centre, and grew to 109 learners from Grade 1 to Matric. By the age of 16, Devon had a C average in Grade 10. His mother Debbie was thrilled.

Debbie: But then you start picking up there are things that are missing – like Afrikaans. He couldn’t speak a word of Afrikaans, but he was passing with 70% and 80%.

V/O: But when Devon was independently assessed, he was found to have the reading competency of an 8 year-old. So how could Devon possibly achieve the marks he did? Grade 10 learner Cameron Eveleigh gave us a clue.

Cameron: When I first got there in Grade 8 and 9, if we were struggling in a test they would literally would just give us the answers.

Bongani: The allegation is they are given the answers as they are writing the tests.

Sheryl: As they are writing the tests?

Bongani: Yes.

Sheryl: I don’t believe that is true for one minute.

Cameron: Kayla and Janine, which were Brenda’s daughters, they used to teach us.

Bongani: Those were your teachers?

Cameron: They taught me Biology, they taught me Geography, they taught me English.

Bongani: Were they the only ones teaching those subjects?

Cameron: Kayla and Janine taught us those subjects, and there were no other teachers involved, except for maybe Sheryl would come in every now and then to check on English.

V/O: Kayla and Jeanine Pieters matriculated from Arvanites College in 2014, and are studying education through UNISA. Sheryl maintains they are just tutors.

Sheryl: So it was last year and this year, 2015 and 2016.

V/O: But Sheryl posted pictures on Facebook of the twins teaching in 2012.

Bongani: And Teaghan who was teaching you?

Teaghan: Mostly for Maths it was a person named Kyle, and the other teacher that teached me the most was Brenda.

Bongani: Is your sister Brenda a qualified teacher?

Sheryl: No.

Bongani: Yet she teaches here at the school?

Sheryl: She doesn’t teach.

Bongani: The parents call Brenda, your sister, a teacher?

Sheryl: That’s what the parents say.

Teaghan: There was actually a time when the teacher would come, she gave me the book with all the answers and she told me to copy from that.

Bongani: Who was that teacher?

Teaghan: That teacher was Brenda.

V/O: And Teagjhan’s Grade 6 report was signed by his teacher, Brenda Pieters. Last year the Gauteng Department of Education knew that some of the teachers weren’t qualifed.

Oupa: That is why we took the action to try to de-register the school.

V/O; Spokesperson Oupa Bodibe explained why the Department’s attempt to de-register the school failed.

Oupa: We didn’t serve the papers to the right people and the lawyers of the school wrote back to say on procedural grounds we appeal that you can’t close the school, and the MEC upheld it, because our officials didn’t do a proper job there.

V/O: Arvanites has now employed new teachers.

Sheryl: Currently there are 68 learners at school, 9 qualified teachers and I think it’s 6 tutors.

V/O: After the matric results debacle Cameron and Teaghan’s mom, Nicky Eveleigh decided to change schools.

Nicky: Randpark High was going to take Cameron back. He made Cameron do 2 exams. They apparently were the same exams he did at Arvanites for the year-end, and he failed both of them dismally. He got 12% for English and 22% for Maths, and on the Arvanitis report he got 64% for English and 40%.

Bongani: A learner writes a test here. They go write the same test a week later at another school and they fail. How do you explain that?

Sheryl: I don’t understand that that happened.

Bongani: So? How do you explain that?

Sheryl: Because I don’t believe that that is entirely true.

Cameron: Despite getting a 70% average at Arvanites, Cameron has had to repeat Grade 10 at Abbotts College.

V/O: Steve Parry had 3 children at Arvanites. His stepson Benjamin Suttie wrote his final matric exams in 2014, but when the matric certificate didn’t arrive, they asked the school to email his results to Stellenbosch University.

Steve: They said well with these marks you’ve got in on the skin of your teeth – but welcome.

V/O; With a Maths mark of 76, and 65 for Physical Science Benjamin was able to enrol for Electrical Engineering.

Benjamin: Maths and Science I knew from my results something wasn’t right. But again they were apparently my final results so you didn’t question.

Steve: She finally said to me I’ve got Ben’s matric statement and this is what she gave me. The watermark isn’t there; It’s off-center; it’s blurred. And her exact words to me were what are you complaining about? You’ve got it haven’t you? So I took this and I sent it off to Verisource. They came back and said this is not a true and correct certificate. So then I sent it off to the Gauteng Department of Education and Umalusi, and they said no, this is not one of ours.

Bongni: So it wasn’t just incorrect, it was inauthentic?

Steve: Yes, it wasn’t worth the paper it was written on. And it had the marks on here that Sheryl Arvanites had sent to the university.

Bongani: This is a certificate you issued to Benjamin Suttie.

Sheryl: I didn't issue this certificate to Benjamin Suttie, this certificate was obtained from the GDE.

Bongani: Does that look like an authentic matric certificate?

Sheryl: This isn't the one we received to start off with.

Bongani: This is the one you issued?

Sheryl: No this isn't, the certificate this learner got didn’t look like this; this is a copy of a certificate.

Bongani: Well of course, it's a copy it's not the original. It’s an exact colour copy.

Sheryl: No it didn't look like this at all.

Steve: I don’t know where this comes from, but it was handed to me in person by Sheryl Arvanites.

Bongani: What were the real results?

Steve: Here, we got this. All the readings were the same except for mathematics, which was supposedly 76. His Maths was 56. Now with 56 you’re not going to get into Stellenbosch. Physical science – it was claimed that he got 65, when he actually got 58. So those are the two that differ.

Sheryl: I don’t believe that those results are fraudulent.

Bongani: This is the real document. Some of these results do not match?

Bongani: I understand that some of these results do not match, but I don't know where they came from, who did what with them, I have no idea.

Bongani: You made this up didn’t you?

Sheryl: No, why would I do that?

V/O: Benjamin failed Mathematics after the first term and had to leave Stellenbosch University.

Steve: We’ve actually laid a charge of fraud against Sheryl Arvanites for issuing this documentation.

Oupa: Obviously there is fraud and there are several allegations of fraud, not just about the qualifications themselves, but also the documents that were used to register the school. That school materially fails to perform above the standards of a public school. The norm last year in Gauteng is that last year we had 82.4% matric pass rate.

V/O: With a 12.5% matric pass rate Arvanites does not meet minimum requirements. On the 26th of April the Department served Arvanites with new papers to de-register the school. They have 30 days to appeal this decision.

Steve: Our daughter who was doing matric last year had to go back 2 years. And my son had to go back one year to Grade 5 again. She needs to be accountable for what she’s done.

Bongani: Sheryl you’re destroying these families’ lives and you show no remorse.

Sheryl: Because I don’t need to be remorseful about something that is not true.

Sheryl: No it didn't look like this at all. Steve: I don’t know where this comes from, but it was handed to me in person by Sheryl Arvanites. Bongani: What were the real results? Steve: Here, we got this. All the readings were the same except for mathematics, which was supposedly 76. His Maths was 56. Now with 56 you’re not going to get into Stellenbosch. Physical science – it was claimed that he got 65, when he actually got 58. So those are the two that differ. Sheryl: I don’t believe that those results are fraudulent. Bongani: This is the real document. Some of these results do not match? Bongani: I understand that some of these results do not match, but I don't know where they came from, who did what with them, I have no idea. Bongani: You made this up didn’t you? Sheryl: No, why would I do that? V/O: Benjamin failed Mathematics after the first term and had to leave Stellenbosch University. Steve: We’ve actually laid a charge of fraud against Sheryl Arvanites for issuing this documentation. Oupa: Obviously there is fraud and there are several allegations of fraud, not just about the qualifications themselves, but also the documents that were used to register the school. That school materially fails to perform above the standards of a public school. The norm last year in Gauteng is that last year we had 82.4% matric pass rate. V/O: With a 12.5% matric pass rate Arvanites does not meet minimum requirements. On the 26th of April the Department served Arvanites with new papers to de-register the school. They have 30 days to appeal this decision. Steve: Our daughter who was doing matric last year had to go back 2 years. And my son had to go back one year to Grade 5 again. She needs to be accountable for what she’s done. Bongani: Sheryl you’re destroying these families’ lives and you show no remorse. Sheryl: Because I don’t need to be remorseful about something that is not true. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Parents pay 4500 Rands a month, but can their children read?
metadata.Summary: Several parents from Arvenites College of Education are outraged after their children failed matrix, and independent evaluations show they are way behind in their education. Many classes are held by "teaching assistants", unqualified teachers who are family of the owners.
metadata.Further information: 14 of the 16 children of the school who wrote matrix have failed 2015 exams. They were excelling with marks between 70% and 80% up until the exams were independently set and marked. Despite several complaints and criminal charges being laid,it;s business as usual at Arvanites
